land.text: the Pentapolis (Cyrene, Apollonia, Taucheira, Euesperides, Barce) that the cyrenaica dossier begins in 332 with Alexander's tribute

successors.note: Cyrene and Barca ends in the year the cyrenaica dossier starts. The Cyrenaica infobox runs the republic to 322 and the Cyrene page has Cyrene outside Macedonian control until Thibron in 324; 332 is the tribute year the cyrenaica dossier uses.

capitals.name: Cyrene (Shahhat)
capitals.note: Chief city of Cyrenaica; Apollonia was its port and Barca a separate city from c. 560.

correction.text: Cyrene and its port, founded in 631 BC by Theran colonists under Battus I

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no row before 331). The pages give no boundary: the radius is the polis and its port. Barca (c. 560) was a separate city founded by exiled brothers of Arcesilaus II, so it is outside this shape.

correction.text: the Pentapolis the Persians seized in 525: Cyrene, Apollonia, Taucheira, Euesperides and Barce

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the Cyrenaica shape of 331 (103 cells, about 26,000 km2) used for the whole span as the Pentapolis. The Cyrenaica page names the cities, gives no area and dates only the Persian seizure (525) and Alexander's tribute (332). How the cities beyond Cyrene came together before 525 is not on any page opened; the gain events say so.

region.text: Cyrene, with its port Apollonia, on the Libyan plateau

ledger.note: 631: Theran settlers under Battus I found Cyrene. 'founded Cyrene in 631 BC, under the leadership of Battus I'; the Battus I page has 'c. 630 BC' and the Cyrenaica infobox 'Kingdom (632-440 BC)'.

region.text: Barce, Euesperides, Taucheira and the land between them, joined to Cyrene as the Pentapolis

ledger.note: 525: the cities of the Pentapolis appear as one unit. Page silent on how Barca (founded c. 560 by exiled brothers of Arcesilaus II, per the Cyrene and Barca pages) and the other cities came under Cyrene: the Cyrenaica page says only that the Persians 'seized the Pentapolis'. Bridging the gap so the Persian vassal has one shape.

region.text: the Pentapolis, a Persian dependency with its own king and then its own republic

ledger.note: 525: the Persians seize the Pentapolis. 'In 525 BC, after conquering Egypt, the Achaemenid (Persian) army of Cambyses II seized the Pentapolis'; the page adds a satrapy over parts of the region for about two centuries, and the Arcesilaus IV page has the Battiad king as 'a client king under Persian authority'.

440: the Battiad monarchy ends. 'Arcesilaus, along with his son, were killed by the Cyrenaean citizens in 440 BC' and the citizens declared a 'narrow democracy'; Cyrenaica infobox 'Kingdom (632-440 BC)', 'Republic (440-322 BC)'. The state, its colour and its Persian dependency continue as a republic.

region.text: the Pentapolis, no longer a Persian dependency

ledger.note: 332: Alexander takes tribute and the Persian dependency ends. 'The Persians were followed by Alexander the Great in 332 BC, who received tribute from the cities after taking Egypt.' The Cyrene page says Cyrene 'did not come under Macedonian control' then, and that Thibron took the port in 324 and Ophellas came in 322.
332: the Pentapolis passes to the cyrenaica dossier. Alexander's tribute (332) opens the Cyrenaica page's Macedonian and Ptolemaic sequence; the republic's own institutions last to 322 (infobox).

wars.name: Egyptian expedition against Cyrene (Battle of Irasa)
wars.outcome: Cyrene victory: Libyan rivals 'appealed to Egypt for help around 570 BC' and the pharaoh Apries 'was decisively defeated at the Battle of Irasa'. No land changed hands.
wars.note: Dated c. 570; the Battus I page mentions Irasa only as farmland on the founders' way to Apollo's Fountain.

wars.name: Battle of Leuco
wars.outcome: Arcesilaus II of Cyrene was killed by the Barcans and Libyans at Leuco around 550 BC; Barca stayed separate until the Persian sack of 515.
wars.note: Barca was founded by the king's brothers after a quarrel; the page does not say where Leuco lay.

wars.name: Persian siege of Barca
wars.outcome: Aryandes, governor of Egypt, 'besieged and sacked Barca in 515 BC' at the call of Pheretime, mother of the murdered Arcesilaus III; Darius I settled some captives in Bactria. The Persian dependency already existed (525).

certainty.note: No page gives a boundary for Cyrene or the Pentapolis; the shapes are the polis radius and the later Cliopatria outline of the five cities.

sources.title: Cyrene, Libya
sources.note: Foundation 631, Battiad reigns, Barca, Irasa 570, Euesperides after 460, Thibron 324, Ophellas 322.

sources.note: Infobox periods (Kingdom 632-440, Republic 440-322), Persian seizure of the Pentapolis 525, Alexander 332.

sources.title: Battus I of Cyrene

sources.title: Arcesilaus IV of Cyrene

notes: Slug cyrene-and-barca is the counterpart the achaemenid-empire dossier already uses (vassal_start 525 'Cyrene and Barca'); eu-01-b's suggested slug 'cyrene' is this dossier. Five pages (the budget is 2-5 for a state with no shapes); Taucheira, Euesperides and Balagrae are named on the Cyrenaica page without dates, so the shapes are polis radius (631-526) and the Pentapolis (525-333). Disagreements: the achaemenid-empire dossier ends its Cyrene and Barca vassal tint in 404 on a page-silent guess; the Cyrenaica page has the Persian satrapy for about two centuries (to 332), which this dossier follows, so achaemenid-empire /ledger vassal_end 404 should move to 332. The Cyrene page says Alexander's conquest of Egypt in 331 left Cyrene outside Macedonian control until Thibron in 324; the Cyrenaica page has tribute in 332. No documented ruler list on the pages: only Battus I 630-600, Arcesilaus II c. 560-550, Battus III c. 550-530, Arcesilaus III c. 530-515, Arcesilaus IV 465-440 are dated, so no rulers strip. Barca (c. 560-515) is not given a dossier of its own; if a gap-filler wants one, the Barca page is the source. Wikipedia 'Cyrene, Libya' is the city's article; the state has no article of its own.
